title: Para completion: where the missing sentence goes

blocks.heading: The format
lines: A sentence and a paragraph with four marked places, (1) to (4). Pick the place where the sentence fits best.
Multiple choice: +3 right, minus 1 wrong. Two in each CAT 2025 slot. About 2 minutes each.

blocks.heading: The method
lines: Read the missing sentence first. Note what it needs before it (a name it uses without introducing, "this", "also", "however") and what it sets up after it.
Read the paragraph once and say in a few words what each sentence does.
Test each place: read the sentence before, the missing sentence, then the sentence after. Both joins must work.
Check that putting it in doesn't break a link already there, such as a "This" that pointed to the sentence before.

blocks.heading: Clues
lines: A pronoun or "this" in the missing sentence: it goes right after the thing it points to.
A pronoun at the start of a paragraph sentence: the missing sentence may be the one that introduces it.
"Also" or "too" needs a similar point just before. "Though" or "however" needs the opposite point.
Dates and stages: the sentence goes where its time fits.
A general claim usually comes before its example, and an example before the lesson drawn from it.

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: The topic matching a place is not enough. The joins on both sides have to work.
Don't split a pair: if the next sentence starts with "This" and points back, nothing can go in between.
Two places still possible: pick the one where the sentence after needs the missing one.
Down to two: answer. Three still possible after 2 minutes: leave it blank.
